If sentiment is >0.67 in the last 3 days, reduce forecast peak by 1.5–2.5% for mid-horizon (days 15–25) to avoid overreaction.  
If sentiment is <0.33 in the last 3 days, increase forecast trough by 1.5–2.5% for early-horizon (days 1–10) to counter pessimism.  
If sentiment swings >0.33 in consecutive days, dampen forecast volatility by 0.5–1.0% across all horizons to smooth overfitting.  
For late-horizon (days 26–30), if sentiment is >0.67, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with diminishing momentum.  
If sentiment is >0.67 and forecast is rising, cap upward slope at 0.5% per day to prevent runaway optimism.  
If sentiment is <0.33 and forecast is falling, offset downward slope with 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent premature collapse.
